title: Critical thinking toolkit
examples: What is the difference between a claim and evidence?
How can I spot an assumption in an argument?
Can an argument be true even if the evidence is weak?

explain.say: A claim is simply a statement that someone believes to be true. It is what the person wants you to accept as fact.
Evidence is the information used to support a claim. It must be factual and can be checked by others.

draw.text: Evidence: Facts to support a claim.

explain.say: An assumption is something taken for granted without proof. It is an unstated belief that the argument relies on.
Consider this claim: all students prefer online learning. The evidence might be recent survey results. The assumption could be that all students use the same devices.

items: Step 1: Claim (All students prefer online learning)
Step 3: Assumption (All students use the same devices)

draw.text: Claim: All students prefer online learning. Evidence: Survey results. Assumption: Same dev

explain.say: In everyday life, if a shop claims apples are the best fruit, their evidence might be a picture. Their assumption could be that you only buy apples.

draw.text: Real-life: Apple claim. Assumption: You only buy apples.

explain.say: A common mistake is confusing a strong assumption with actual evidence. Always ask yourself what is not being shown to you.

draw.text: Mistake: Confusing assumption with evidence. Fix: Ask what is missing.

faq.q: What is the difference between an assumption and a belief?
faq.a: A belief is just what someone feels is true. An assumption is a belief that the speaker treats as if it were a proven fact for their argument to work.
asks: How are assumptions different from opinions?
Is every assumption also a belief?

faq.q: Do I need evidence for every single claim I make?
faq.a: For strong arguments, yes, you should always try to back up your claims with solid evidence. If you cannot, you must state it is just your opinion.
asks: Can I make a claim without proof?
When is it okay to make an unsupported claim?

faq.q: How do I find the assumption when I read an article?
faq.a: Read the argument slowly and ask yourself what must be true for the conclusion to make sense. That missing piece is often the assumption.
asks: What is the best way to find hidden assumptions?
Should I look for assumptions in the introduction?

faq.q: Is it possible for the evidence to be true but the claim to be false?
faq.a: Yes, this is possible. The evidence might be accurate, but the person might misinterpret it to create a false claim.
asks: Does true evidence guarantee a true claim?

faq.a: Good evidence is usually factual, comes from reliable sources, and is directly related to the claim being made. Personal stories are sometimes weak evidence.

facts: A claim is a statement that something is true.
Evidence provides facts to support a claim.
An assumption is something taken for granted without proof.
Arguments rely on claims, evidence, and assumptions working together.

quiz.say: The claim is that recycling saves energy. The evidence is that a local plant uses less electricity. The assumption is that all energy sources are equally efficient.
quiz.show: Claim: Recycling saves energy. Evidence: Local plant uses less electricity. Assumption: All energy sources are equally efficient.

options.show: The plant is in the city.
options.say: The plant is in the city.

options.show: All energy sources are equally efficient.
options.say: All energy sources are equally efficient.

quiz.why: The argument assumes that the efficiency of energy sources is the same across the board for the claim to hold true.

wrong.0: This is the evidence provided to support the claim.
wrong.1: This detail is extra information and not the core missing assumption.
wrong.3: This is the main claim, not the unstated assumption.

quiz.say: A politician claims that new laws will help the economy. The evidence is a graph showing past growth. The assumption is that the current economic problems are temporary.
quiz.show: Claim: New laws help economy. Evidence: Past growth graph. Assumption: Current problems are temporary.

options.show: New laws will help the economy.
options.say: New laws will help the economy.

quiz.why: The politician must assume the current downturn is temporary for the new laws to be the correct solution.

wrong.1: This is the conclusion or claim, not the hidden assumption.
wrong.2: This is the evidence presented, not the assumption.
wrong.3: While this might be a bias, the core logical assumption is about the state of the economy.
